conventions.userPortalTransport: Authenticated browser calls go to same-origin BFF routes (browser-api.ts rewrites backend-shaped paths); BFFs attach the bearer token from HttpOnly __Host- cookies. Anonymous operations without secrets may go browser-direct to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL with the public tenant header. Server Components use private API_BASE_URL via server-api.ts.
conventions.adminPortalTransport: Only sign-in/refresh/logout BFFs exist. Admin data reads/mutations need new server reads/BFF routes; mutations also need step-up (SHARED.admin-verify-step-up).
conventions.tenant: Tenant header comes from app configuration (TENANT_ID_HEADER); admin list endpoints additionally accept tenantId filters.
conventions.errors: Transport normalizes ApiError; apps map status/stable codes; validation problems map to fields where known.

gaps.title: Checked-in OpenAPI reference is far behind the backend
gaps.observed: backendprojecttemplatewebapi.json lists 21 operations; backend 1fcad50 has 100 controller endpoints (80 absent from the file). 31 of 48 frontend operations are not in the file, and it still documents POST /api/v1/stakeholders/me/profile/avatar, which the backend no longer exposes (replaced by avatar/uploads + complete). All 48 frontend operation methods/paths match the backend.
gaps.desired: Refresh the reference with pnpm sync:openapi against the recorded backend revision in a separately authorized change; review the diff; no code generation.
gaps.prerequisite: Running backend at the recorded commit.
acceptanceCriteria: Spec operation set equals backend controller set (webhooks may be included).
No TypeScript generated; handwritten contracts unchanged unless a real drift is found.
tests: Manual diff review; existing api-client HTTP-boundary tests stay green.
gaps.sequencing: First; makes later admin/KYC contract work reviewable.
relatedTickets: CAF-FE-001 (named in the brief; not found in repository text)

gaps.title: Admin step-up MFA is enforced by the backend but absent in the frontend
gaps.observed: Every admin mutation (lock/unlock, role assign/remove, session revoke(s), plan create/update/activation, subscription allocate/cancel/retry, payment-provider activation, active provider) carries [RequireStepUpMfa] and needs X-Step-Up-Authorization from POST /api/v1/authentication/security/step-up/verifications. AdminStepUpDialog is presentation-only; no api-client operation; setPaymentProviderActivation/setActiveProvider cannot send the header; OKF authentication domain states 'no step-up endpoint or admin MFA exists' (stale).
gaps.desired: api-client operation for step-up verification; per-operation optional step-up header parameter; admin BFF routes that obtain and attach the proof server-side; dialog wired to verify with authenticator codes only.
gaps.prerequisite: GAP-017-003 (admins must be able to sign in with MFA).
acceptanceCriteria: Proof requested with the exact method/path/query/body of the intended mutation.
Proof/token never stored, logged or exposed to browser JS beyond the BFF.
Stable mfa_* errors mapped; consumed proofs never retried.
tests: HTTP-boundary tests for the new operation and header.
BFF route tests for proof attach and error mapping.
Dialog browser test (code entry, error, cancel).
gaps.sequencing: After GAP-017-003; before any admin mutation adapter.
relatedTickets: Proposed new card (no existing owner found)

gaps.title: Admin Portal cannot complete MFA sign-in
gaps.observed: apps/admin-portal/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts returns 409 two_factor_required ('not available in the admin portal yet'). Step-up requires an enrolled authenticator (mfa_enrollment_required), so an admin able to perform privileged mutations cannot sign in, and there is no admin enrollment surface.
gaps.desired: Admin two-factor challenge continuation (reuse the User Portal challenge-cookie pattern) and a decided enrollment path for admins.
gaps.prerequisite: Product decision on where admins enroll MFA.
acceptanceCriteria: MFA-enrolled admin can sign in; challenge stored only in HttpOnly cookie; role admission applied after challenge success.
tests: BFF tests for challenge set/verify/clear; browser test for the two-factor step.
relatedTickets: Proposed new card (no existing owner found)

gaps.title: Admin admission and per-permission UX do not reflect backend roles
gaps.observed: Admission checks one JWT role claim (ADMIN_REQUIRED_ROLE). Backend has four seeded roles (Administrator, ComplianceOfficer, FinanceOfficer, SupportAgent) and evaluates permissions per request from current Identity membership, ignoring JWT role claims. No endpoint returns the caller's effective permissions, so UI must treat a 403 per section as hide/disable (BE-DS-002 rule).
gaps.desired: Decide admission (any admin role vs one); per-section 403 handling via AdminForbidden/section states; optional backend 'my permissions' read to avoid probing.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-Administrator roles can be admitted when intended.
A 403 on one section never fails the whole page.
tests: proxy/admission unit tests per role claim; section-level 403 tests.
relatedTickets: Backend enhancement proposal (optional) — no existing owner found

gaps.title: Password-reset request BFF body reveals whether the email exists
gaps.observed: On a known email the BFF passes through the backend 202 body {message: 'If the account is eligible, a password reset OTP will be sent shortly.'} (PasswordResetsController.cs:49); on an unknown email it converts the backend 404 into 202 with its own fixed PASSWORD_RESET_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE 'If the account is eligible, a password reset code will be sent shortly.' (password-reset-bff.ts:20-21). Status codes match and on-screen copy is identical, but the HTTP bodies differ ('OTP' vs 'code'), so the response still enumerates accounts to anyone reading the network response. Raised as an open item by FE-UI-016.
gaps.desired: The request BFF always returns the fixed accepted message (never the backend body) for both outcomes; the completion BFF likewise returns fixed bodies.
gaps.prerequisite: None (independent of BE-DS-006, which removes the backend 404).
acceptanceCriteria: Known and unknown emails produce byte-identical 202 response bodies and the same headers from the BFF.
tests: BFF route test asserting identical bodies for backend 202 and backend 404.
